notes.mod_writer:
**DslWriter**

Every model edit becomes a Roslyn `DocumentEditor` rewrite here. Never a string rebuild, never `NormalizeWhitespace()` — both destroy trivia, and trivia is what makes a diff readable.

If the round-trip fixtures fail, this file is wrong. Not the test.
notes.mod_engine:
**StemmaEngine**

The façade the web layer is allowed to call, and the boundary the purity rule defends. It references Roslyn and `Stemma.Model`. It does not know that HTTP exists.
notes.sys_git:
**Git working tree**

The store. `Architecture/*.cs` and `Views/*.cs` are the model; `stemma.layout.json` is presentation. Branch, blame, revert and review all work because there is nothing else to keep in sync.
notes.mod_render:
**DiagramRenderer**

Drives a bare canvas through Playwright and screenshots the content bounds. Starts a short-lived host per render, which is why two renders never fight over one workspace.

It exits `0` whatever it drew — see `risk_exitzero`.
notes.mod_hub:
**SignalR hub**

The operation stream in, the delta broadcast out. Modelled as one `twoway` flow rather than two arrows because it is one round trip.
notes.con_fidelity:
The rule that outranks every other argument in this repository.

It is not a policy document. It is `DslWriter` plus minimal, realistic and deliberately pathological fixtures per operation.

ships.title: Four things ship
ships.narrative:
Start here. A web host, a canvas in the browser, a command-line tool and a desktop
window that wraps the first two. Underneath sit the only two things Stemma cannot do
without: Roslyn, which reads and rewrites the C#, and a Git working tree, which is
where the model lives. There is no database on this picture because there is no
database anywhere.

diff.title: A gesture becomes a diff
diff.narrative:
Follow the top row left to right, then drop down and come back along the bottom. You
rename a box on the canvas, the canvas sends one operation over SignalR, the hub hands
it to the engine, the engine goes through DslWriter, DslWriter asks Roslyn for a
targeted edit, and Roslyn writes Architecture.cs. Seven hops, and the last one is a
line in `git diff`. The dashed arrow going back to Roslyn is the read path: the same
file, parsed, is where the model came from in the first place.

engine.title: What the engine is allowed to know
engine.narrative:
The facade on the left, its leaves on the right, and nothing pointing back. The engine
references Roslyn and the record vocabulary and nothing else — not the web layer, not
the client, not an HTTP type. That constraint is why the fidelity suite can test the
whole write path without starting a server, and it is the first thing to check when a
new feature wants to reach for a convenience.

book_review.name: Why the diff is worth trusting

rules.title: Three rules that win arguments
rules.narrative:
These are not aspirations. Each one has something on the right that enforces it, and
when a rule and a feature disagree, the rule wins and the feature gets redesigned.
The middle row is the one people push back on hardest: everything that is not the C#
model lives in one committed sidecar, and a third store has been proposed and refused
more than once.

guarantee.title: Where the guarantee actually lives
guarantee.narrative:
The guarantee is not a policy, it is DslWriter plus the fixtures behind it. A rename
rewrites the declaration and the references Roslyn can see, and touches nothing else:
no reordering, no reformatting, no lost comment. Every operation carries minimal,
realistic and deliberately pathological round-trip fixtures, and when they fail the
implementation is wrong, not the test.

unsure.title: What I am not sure about
unsure.narrative:
The honest slide. A risk, an open question and a standing assumption, each anchored to
the thing it concerns rather than filed in a wiki nobody opens. The assumption at the
bottom is the one everything else rests on: if the source on disk stops being the
model, none of the rest of this argument survives.

command.title: One command, no browser
command.narrative:
This is the half with no person in it. An agent writes three text files by hand,
runs `stemma render`, and the CLI starts a short-lived host of its own, drives a bare
canvas through Chromium, and writes a PNG next to a manifest. The short-lived host is
the reason two renders never fight over one workspace.

manifest.title: The manifest is the point
manifest.narrative:
The image is the boring output. The manifest beside it fingerprints the model, the
view, the layout and the profile it was drawn from, so `stemma render --check` can
tell a build that a committed picture has stopped matching its source. That is the
"cannot drift" claim extended past the app window, and it is the thing a drawing tool
structurally cannot offer.
